quiz.title: CBSE Class 12 Maths 2009 Paper Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight board-level questions in the style of the 2009 paper, spanning calculus, matrices and determinants, integrals, differential equations, vectors, 3D geometry and probability. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If y = x<sup>x</sup>, then dy/dx equals:
questions.explanation: Take logs: log y = x log x. Differentiating, (1/y) dy/dx = log x + 1, so dy/dx = x<sup>x</sup>(1 + log x).

questions.q: If A is a 3 × 3 matrix with det(A) = 4, then det(2A) equals:
questions.explanation: For an n × n matrix, det(kA) = k<sup>n</sup> det(A). Here det(2A) = 2<sup>3</sup> × 4 = 8 × 4 = 32.
∫ tan x dx = −log|cos x| + C = log|sec x| + C, since sec x = 1/cos x.

questions.q: The degree of the differential equation (d<sup>2</sup>y/dx<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> + (dy/dx)<sup>3</sup> = x is:
questions.explanation: Degree is the power of the highest-order derivative once the equation is polynomial in derivatives. The highest order is d<sup>2</sup>y/dx<sup>2</sup> and it is raised to the power 2, so the degree is 2.

questions.q: If |a| = 3, |b| = 4 and a · b = 6, the angle between a and b is:
A line makes equal angles with all three coordinate axes. Each of its direction cosines is:
questions.explanation: If l = m = n and l<sup>2</sup> + m<sup>2</sup> + n<sup>2</sup> = 1, then 3l<sup>2</sup> = 1, giving each direction cosine as 1/√3.

questions.q: If A and B are independent events with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.6, then P(A ∩ B) equals:
questions.explanation: For independent events, P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B) = 0.3 × 0.6 = 0.18.

questions.q: ∫ from −1 to 1 of x<sup>3</sup> dx equals:
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup> is an odd function, and the integral of an odd function over a symmetric interval [−a, a] is 0.

faq.q: What topics does the CBSE Class 12 Mathematics 2009 paper cover?
faq.a: It spans the Class 12 syllabus of that year — differentiation and integration, matrices and determinants, vectors and three-dimensional geometry, differential equations, linear programming and probability. That same spread still forms the core of the board paper today.

faq.q: Is the 2009 paper still useful for the current CBSE exam?
faq.a: Yes. The format has since added MCQ and case-study sections, but the underlying concepts are unchanged. The 2009 paper is clean, well-set practice for building accuracy in calculus, algebra and vectors before you move to a current sample paper.

faq.q: How is the 2009 paper different from a recent board paper?
faq.a: The 2009 paper uses the older scheme of mainly short- and long-answer questions, with no objective or case-based section. Use it for concept drill, then rehearse the present-day pattern with a recent sample paper.

faq.q: What is the best way to practise with a previous-year paper?
faq.a: Attempt it in one timed sitting without notes, mark it honestly against the answer key, then re-solve only the questions you got wrong. That gap analysis fixes weak spots far better than reading through solved answers.
